investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-08-13T00:39–00:47Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported it as exhausted, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the Pending state, so the eval runner could not reach the agent creation or readiness steps required by the expected-output contract.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted the schedulable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry it. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) confirms that no node can accept a new peer-pod VM at this time and preemption cannot help. This is an infrastructure-layer capacity constraint, not an application code defect. The eval failure is a direct consequence: because the pod never schedules, createAgent() in run-status-probes.mjs never returns a VM ID or remote state, and all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) remain absent (evidence: expected-output.missing-required-evidence).

Supported by the explicit 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' message in all three sibling check failures (failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime).

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch on the remaining 4 nodes: the remote-agent pod spec requires a label or taint that only the 2 kata-capable nodes carry, so even if VM slots were available on other nodes, the pod could not be placed there. This is a configuration constraint, not a capacity leak.

Quaternary — a node running kata.peerpods.io/vm became unavailable or was cordoned, reducing effective capacity from a higher baseline to the 2 nodes observed. No node-health or cluster-event signals are present to confirm this.

investigation.title: Remote Agent Pods Unschedulable Due to Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity — All Three Remote-Agent Checks Failing
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place new pods: only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both are fully exhausted, while the remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. Because no pod was ever scheduled, the agent was never created, and the remote-agent-state eval received zero evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state all missing), violating its expected-output contract.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity across the 2 eligible nodes. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" confirms that no schedulable capacity exists and preemption cannot help. Because the eval probe calls createAgent(..., "remote", ...) at run-status-probes.mjs line 1905, and that call depends on a pod reaching a running state, the probe timed out after ~148 s without ever producing the required evidence fields. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity failure localized to the remote-agent VM pool; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-08-13T00:39–00:47Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported it as exhausted, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the Pending state, so the eval runner could not reach the agent creation or readiness steps required by the expected-output contract.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted the schedulable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry it. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) confirms that no node can accept a new peer-pod VM at this time and preemption cannot help. This is an infrastructure-layer capacity constraint, not an application code defect. The eval failure is a direct consequence: because the pod never schedules, createAgent() in run-status-probes.mjs never returns a VM ID or remote state, and all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) remain absent (evidence: expected-output.missing-required-evidence).

sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical scheduler error, pod stuck 147s, status=fail — confirms the constraint persisted across the full eval window (~7 minutes, 00:39–00:47Z).
